title: Protocol for the use of _Polylox_ – endogenous barcoding for high resolution in vivo lineage tracing
protocol: Set up timed matings between Rosa26<sup>Polylox/Polylox</sup> and Tie2<sup>MCM/+</sup> mice.
Treat pregnant mice with a single dose of 2.5 mg tamoxifen and 1.25 mg progesterone orally on day 9.5 by gavage.
Prepare tamoxifen stock solution by dissolving 1 g tamoxifen in 4 ml absolute ethanol and 36 ml peanut oil at 55 °C.
Store tamoxifen stock solution at -20°C.
Deliver pups via caesarean section on E20.5 and raise them by foster mothers.
Genotype the pups for the Tie2<sup>MCM</sup> allele using primers #972, #984, and #HL14 at 3-4 weeks after birth from genomic DNA prepared from tail biopsies.
Perform PCR on genomic DNA of Ficoll-separated peripheral blood leukocytes to test successful tamoxifen induction in Rosa26<sup>Polylox/+</sup>Tie2<sup>MCM/+</sup> mice using primers #2450 and #2427.
Separate PCR products by gel electrophoresis.
Prepare tamoxifen stock solution by dissolving 1 g tamoxifen in 4 ml absolute ethanol.
Dissolve the mixture with 36 ml peanut oil at 55 °C.
Inject adult _Rosa26<sup>Polylox/+</sup>Tie2<sup>MCM/+</sup>_ mice intraperitoneally with 1 mg tamoxifen on five consecutive days.
Test successful tamoxifen induction of _Rosa26<sup>Polylox/+</sup>Tie2<sup>MCM/+</sup>_ mice by PCR amplification of the _Polylox_ locus.
Sacrifice mice by carbon dioxide inhalation on the day of analysis.
Harvest peritoneal exudate cells by lavage of the peritoneal cavity with 5% FACS buffer for 5 times using 2 ml each time.
Use plastic Pasteur pipettes to gently lavage and avoid injury and blood cell contamination.
Take out the spleen and cut it into small pieces in 5% FACS buffer using surgical scissors.
Pass the minced spleen through a 40-μm filter using 5% FACS buffer and the plunger of a 5-ml syringe to obtain single splenocytes.
Prepare femora and tibiae for bone marrow recovery.
Flush bone marrow cells from long bones with 5% FACS buffer or crush all bones in a mortar in 5% FACS buffer.
Resuspend extracted bone marrow cells by repeated pipetting.
Filter resuspended bone marrow cells through a 40-μm mesh to remove remaining bone pieces.
Determine the concentration of cell suspensions using an automated cell counter according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Incubate 5x10^6 cells/50 μl with 300 μg/ml whole mouse IgG for 15 min to block Fc receptors.
Add cocktails with titrated concentrations of fluorescent dye-labeled antibodies in 5% FACS buffer and stain the cells for 45 min in the dark on ice.
Wash stained cells with an appropriate amount of 5% FACS buffer.
Add 100 nM SYTOX Blue at least 5 min before analysis to exclude dead cells.
Filter cell suspensions through a snap cap cell strainer mash to remove clumps before placing them on the FACS sorter.
Analyze stained cells on a FACSAriaIII cell sorter running BD FACSDiva software and sort populations of interest into 20% FACS collection buffer (DPBS containing 20% FBS).
Alternatively, directly sort cells into PCR buffer.
Aliquot sorted cells and reanalyze aliquots to determine sort purity.
Deposit individual cells into 8-tube PCR stripes containing 25 μl of 1x PCR buffer supplemented with 12.6 μg Proteinase K by FACS sorting.
Perform lysis for 1 hour at 55 °C, then terminate the reaction at 95 °C for 10 minutes and cool down to 4 °C.
Add remaining PCR reagents to reach a final volume of 50 μl.
Initiate first round PCR using primers #2450 and #494: start with 5 min at 95 °C, followed by \(30 s at 95 °C, 30 s at 56 °C, 5 min at 72 °C) repeated 35 times; end with 10 min at 72 °C.

Use 1-2 μl of the first PCR reaction as template for second round PCR using primers #2426 and #2427: start with 5 min at 95 °C, followed by \(30 s at 95 °C, 30 s at 62 °C, 5 min at 72 °C) repeated 35 times; end with 10 min at 72 °C.
Analyze nested PCR products by gel electrophoresis for product length.
Send the nested PCR products for Sanger sequencing (e.g., GATC Biotech).
Sort cells into 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes containing 300 μl of 20% FACS buffer.
Use 2-5% of the sorted cells for reanalysis and harvest remaining cells by centrifugation at 1500 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Turn the tube 180° in the rotor and spin again for 5 min at 1500 g.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend with 25 μl lysis buffer (1x PCR buffer 1 from the Expand Long Template PCR system in water and 12.6 μg Proteinase K).
Digest at 55 °C for 1 hour.
Terminate the reaction at 95 °C for 10 min.
Store DNA at -20 °C.
Sort cells into 2 ml FACS collection buffer (20%).
Harvest cell pellet by centrifuging at 400 g for 10 min after reanalysis for sort purity.
Carefully remove the supernatant, leaving 50-100 μl to avoid disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μl freshly prepared proteinase K solution (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 5 mM EDTA, 1% SDS, 0.3 M Na-acetate, 0.2 mg/ml proteinase K).
Incubate at 37 °C for at least 3 hours.
Purify genomic DNA from the lysate by phenol-chloroform extraction.
Extract once with an equal volume of a 1:1 mixture of phenol and chloroform.
Extract the aqueous phase at least twice with an equal volume of chloroform.
Precipitate the DNA by adding 1/10 volume of Na-acetate (3M) pH 5, 1 volume of isopropanol, and 5-20 μg glycogen for 1 hour at –20 °C.
Spin at 16000 g for 10 min.
Wash the DNA pellet twice with 75% ethanol.
Dissolve the air-dried pellet in water.
Measure DNA concentration.
Amplify _Polylox_ cassette from 100-200 ng of template DNA by PCR using described conditions.
Observe one third of the PCR reaction products by gel electrophoresis.
Use the entire PCR product left after gel electrophoresis for an initial AMPure PB bead clean up step, following manufacturer’s protocol.
Determine DNA concentration by Qubit measurement.
Perform a Bioanalyzer run according to manufacturers’ protocols.
Continue library preparation for PacBio SMRT sequencing according to the company’s protocol.
Perform primer annealing and polymerase binding as per manufacturer's instructions.
Load the library by Magbead mode on PacBio RS II or diffusion mode on PacBio Sequel for SMRT sequencing.
Check experimentally found barcodes with the complete list of possible barcodes.
Purge erroneous barcodes from the list if necessary.
Determine the minimal number of recombinations for each barcode by looking up in a pre-calculated table.
Calculate the frequency distribution of recombination events.
Use the frequency distribution to calculate generation probabilities for all barcodes.
